A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiT training results, attention analyses, head ablations, embedding interventions, and prompt-robustness experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds weight-space screening, CLIP-DiT experiments, further robustness analyses, and a pretrained PixArt-Sigma evaluation.

M1.justification: v2 adds a weight-space head-screening algorithm that combines positional queries with relation-feature keys and ranks heads through directional-ramp alignment (Section 5, Appendix B.7). This substantially extends v1's attention-synopsis and targeted QK inspection procedures, allowing systematic screening without generating images.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained synthetic two-object task and filler-word variations, v2 evaluates locative inversion and color synonyms (Appendix A.8). It also introduces natural-object prompts covering 30 object pairs for pretrained PixArt-Sigma, extending actual evaluation beyond synthetic shapes (Appendix A.10).

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the existing RTE and T5 comparison configurations and adds one encoder family, CLIP, at DiT-B and DiT-mini sizes under the same prompt templates. Renamed random-embedding configurations match the earlier comparators.

E3.justification: The new PixArt-Sigma evaluation introduces object-order and relation-reversal controls, SAM detection plus annotation, and relation accuracy conditioned on correct objects (Figure 30). The embedding-intervention multiplier changes from 2 to 3, and Appendix B.5 revises the stated attention-synopsis sweep from 168 to 96 prompts; this reporting revision does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendices A.7–A.10 add screening across model configurations, analyses connecting prompt perturbations to embeddings and spatial gradients, CLIP token and head ablations, and a pretrained-model case study. These substantially extend the mechanistic and robustness evidence. The original RTE ablations remain, despite being merged into different figures.

E5.justification: Figure 30A newly specifies 100 generation seeds for the pretrained-model evaluation. This is additional seed-count information, not evidence of increased repetitions for existing experiments. The original Table 2 sampling description and Appendix B.6 permutation-testing procedure are retained.

E6.justification: Existing Table 2 results are unchanged, but CLIP results are added: DiT-mini loose spatial accuracy is 0.814 on the original template and 0.819 with 'the' before object 2. New findings identify T5 L3H7 and CLIP L0H2/L0H5, show substantial effects of CLIP head ablation, and report nontrivial pretrained performance for 8 of 30 object pairs. The vector-intervention illustration is also replaced under different scaling.

T1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds a substantial mathematical formulation of head screening (Equations 27–38), including the positional-embedding approximation for queries, spatial QK maps, directional ramp templates, and aggregate head scores. The earlier variance-partition derivation remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and Discussion retain the same central claims about encoder-dependent spatial circuits, attention analysis, and differing prompt robustness. The added methods and experiments expand their support without changing these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains how T5 heads produce spatial gradients from relation factors in object tokens and connects perturbations to distorted gradients and biased placement. It also adds substantive qualifications: zero-sum factorization can bias feature discovery, screened heads require causal validation, CLIP ablations also harm object attributes, and pretrained transfer remains limited (Appendices A.8–A.10 and B.6–B.7).

D1.justification: v1 promises code and data release after acceptance; v2 supplies a repository address and states that code, configurations, and datasets are available. It also documents the CLIP checkpoint, precision and embedding dimensions, provides screening pseudocode, and newly identifies Table 2's 4000-epoch EMA checkpoint.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fel et al.'s 'Into the rabbit hull' citation when discussing alternative spatial query representations. Appendices B.6–B.7 also briefly position variance partitioning as supervised feature discovery relative to sparse autoencoders. The existing background and principal novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Section 5 receives localized rewriting, Appendix B.6 gains intuitive exposition, and the earlier robustness discussion moves into Appendix A.8. Terminology is revised toward RTE naming. The abstract, introduction, Discussion, and main section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 3–5 and 7 are substantially recomposed with additional panels. v1's Figure 6 ablations become panels in v2's Figures 4–5, while its Figure 9 moves to Figure 26. New screening, robustness, CLIP, and pretrained-model figures and an expanded Table 2 substantially extend the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 left the specific T5 relation-head mechanism unresolved. v2 substantially closes that gap through weight-space localization and perturbation analysis, strengthens generality with causal CLIP experiments, and adds an initial pretrained-model check. Detailed screening instructions and reported code/data availability also improve reproducibility. Pretrained head causality remains unvalidated, and localized reporting inconsistencies remain, including the alignment sign in Appendix A.8 versus Figure 27, but the mechanistic and evidential gains are substantial.
